findings.message: The pusher's display name ("Pushed by Maya Fernando") is written as free text into `agents.suggestion.detail`. That row's retention entry lists only `acts_for`, `first_approved_by`, `decided_by` and `undone_by` as subjects, and `detail` is neither a field nor a `subjectName`. As a result, an erasure request or legal hold for the pusher never finds this row, and their name stays in someone else's suggestion. The label is also copied when the suggestion is created instead of being read from the record, so a later rename is never reflected. Fix: store the pusher id (`pushedBy`) in `proposed` or `evidence`, which the retention entry already covers, and resolve the name when the suggestion is shown. Do not save the name in `detail`.
findings.rule: docs/module-standard.md (personal data has a retention rule) / 032 erasure
findings.scenario: CI pushes for Maya and Nimal gets a suggestion that says "Pushed by Maya Fernando". Maya's erasure request is approved and completed, and Nimal's suggestion still shows her name for up to a year.

findings.message: Round 2 stops untrusted drafts from claiming whole days, but they can still claim single commits. A service credential (CI) may draft for every author, and it claims a person's commit ids in `commit_draft` under that person's user_id, with whatever `at` it sent. When the person later pushes the same commits with the real times, or a provider-verified webhook carries a `Time:` line for them, nothing is drafted. If the person dismisses the CI suggestion as "not mine" (which the README now invites), the claim stays and those hours can never be drafted again. Fix: an untrusted pusher's claim must not block the person's own push or the webhook. For example, release the claims when the suggestion is dismissed, or keep claims per pusher and let the person's own path take over.
findings.scenario: CI syncs Nimal's commit X with a wrong `at`, and a 0.5 h suggestion is drafted. Nimal dismisses it. Nimal's own sync then carries X at its real time and returns `drafted: 0`, and X's hours are lost for good.

findings.message: Hours are estimated twice and the two results can disagree. The first `daysFor` over all commits decides what to claim. The second `daysFor` runs over only the claimed commits and produces the hours that get drafted. A session that is cut by the 'today' boundary, or by commits another path already claimed, is therefore re-estimated as separate lone commits. The drafted hours then depend on when the pushes happen, not on the commits. A won commit can also land on a day that the re-estimate rounds to 0 h: it is claimed but appears in no draft. Fix: draft the first estimate's per-day hours for the days whose commits this transaction won. Do not re-estimate a subset.
findings.scenario: UTC author, commit A at 23:30 on Nov 10 and commit B at 00:45 on Nov 11. A single sync on Nov 12 drafts 1 h + 0.75 h = 1.75 h. If instead one sync runs at noon on Nov 11 and another on Nov 12, the drafts are 0.5 h (A alone) + 0.5 h (B alone) = 1.0 h.

findings.message: The `day`-only input form skips the consent-period check (`input.at &&` …), so a day from before `since` still drafts. No production caller uses this form any more. Either remove it, or compare `input.day` against the consent start's day as well.
findings.scenario: draftCommitTime({ day: "2026-10-01", … }) with consent from 2026-11-05 → drafted: true

findings.message: `/\(#\d+\)\s*$/` on the subject treats any hand-written issue reference at the end of a subject as a squash. The table test covers this case only in the body.
findings.scenario: "specclaw(101-export): fix rounding (#12)" written by hand on a branch → foldsCommits true → its hours are never drafted

findings.message: The docs disagree with the code. The README still says hours are estimated "per proposal and UTC day", but days are now the author's own zone. In `module.ts` (around line 78), the retention comment still calls the row "the 'drafted once' key for that person's day", but round 2 dropped that key. `contracts.ts` still says `day` is the commit's date in UTC, but the webhook now uses the author's day. The `CommitTime` contract also gains `pushedBy` without the README note that module-standard requires for a contract change.

Round 2 relies on one claim per commit in `delivery.commit_draft`. The key it claims is the raw `id` string, and the push accepts any sha that is 7 to 40 hex characters in either case (`push.ts:33`, `SHA_RE` is `/i`). Nothing normalises it. The webhook claims the provider's full lowercase sha, so the same commit gets a different key when the sync sends it short or in capitals. The pusher controls the payload. Duplicates inside one payload also slip through: `claim` wins the id once, but `commits.filter((c) => won.has(c.id))` keeps both copies, so `commits` and `ids` count it twice. Fix: in `CommitInput`, accept only a full 40-character sha and lowercase it, and make the claim and the estimate use the same de-duplicated id list. Do the same for the `commit` input of `draftCommitTime`. Add a table test over full, short, uppercase and repeated-in-one-payload ids.
findings.scenario: The webhook drafts commit `ab12cd3...` (40 characters, lowercase) from its `Time:` line. A later sync, or CI, sends the same commit as `AB12CD3` (7 characters, upper) → `on conflict` doesn't fire, so a second suggestion is drafted for the same work. The same happens when one push lists the same commit twice: the draft says `commits: 2` with `ids [a, a]`.

findings.message: The retention comment says the row is "the 'drafted once' key for that person's day". Round 2 removed that key: rows are now one per draft, and `commit_draft` holds the claim. The header comment in `sync-time.ts` (lines 11-12) has the same mistake ("one per person, proposal and day"). Update both comments.
